sections.h2: Where is Waukee and how fast has it grown?
sections.html:
Waukee is a Dallas County city on the west side of the Des Moines metro, and it has been one of the fastest-growing places in Iowa. The town was laid out in 1869 and incorporated in 1878, and it is believed to be named after the Milwaukee Road Railroad.

YearPopulation
19701,577
20005,126
201013,790
202023,940
2024 estimate34,420

That makes Waukee the 16th-largest city in Iowa. The area is about 22 square miles at an elevation of 1,047 feet. Growth that quick means a large share of the houses are likely newer, and owners of older homes sit among many recent builds.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show for Waukee households?
sections.html:
Waukee is a high-income, highly educated city with a median home value of $350,500. The Census Bureau reports a 66.5 percent owner-occupied rate for 2020 to 2024, and median gross rent of $1,383.

  • Median household income: $101,029 in 2024 dollars
  • Bachelor's degree or higher, ages 25 and up: 58.0 percent
  • Persons per household: 2.46
  • Mean travel time to work: 19.8 minutes

The median age was 33.9 in the 2020 census, so the typical household here is young. The one-third of occupied homes that are rented also means landlords and investors are active, and a fair share of Waukee sellers own a house they no longer live in.

Apple is the headline. In 2017 the company chose Waukee for a $1.38 billion data center campus, and the city's 2026 development list still shows an Apple site plan (Project Morgan) for a laydown area at West Hickman Road and Northwest 30th Street.

Retail and services are growing too. The same list includes a Walmart Supercenter site plan near Northeast Alice's Road and East Hickman Road, a Hy-Vee expansion within The Crossing at Alice's Road, and a Mid-American substation. Projects like these show the city is still building out its commercial base.

sections.h2: How many new homes is Waukee adding?
sections.html:
The city's 2026 project tracker shows plats, rezonings and site plans for both single-family and multi-family housing. Examples include The South 60 Plat 1 (single-family) near Hickman Road, Trailridge Creek Plat 2 (single and multi-family), Alderbrook (single-family, townhome and commercial) and Sugar Creek Landing.

  • Townhome projects include Maple Street Village and Triumph Village.
  • Multi-family projects include The Wren and Caliber Kettlestone.
  • Growth areas cluster around Kettlestone, Grand Prairie Parkway and Alice's Road.

If you want to sell an existing house here, new construction is part of the competition, since buyers can compare your house with homes still being platted.

sections.h2: What is the Waukee Community School District?
sections.html:
The Waukee Community School District describes itself as the fastest-growing district in Iowa, with more than 13,600 students from preschool through grade 12 and over 2,200 staff. It covers about 55 square miles and also serves students from Clive, Urbandale and West Des Moines, along with open-enrollment students.

It runs 10 elementary schools, four middle schools, Waukee High School and Waukee Northwest High School, which opened for the 2021 school year. Confirm your attendance area before listing, since boundaries cross city lines.

sections.h2: How do people get around Waukee?
sections.html:
Waukee had no fixed-route transit as of 2023 and was the largest city in Iowa without it. HIRTA provides demand-response service, and the Des Moines Area Regional Transit Route 92 express serves Clive, about half a mile away.

Most households therefore rely on cars, so garage space and street access count more here than in a city with frequent bus service. Triangle Park in downtown Waukee and Waukee Stadium are among the local landmarks.

sections.h2: What permits does the city of Waukee require?
sections.html:
Waukee runs most permits through an online portal. Its list of building permits covers single-family additions and alterations, accessory buildings, fences, decks, residential pools, hot tubs, signs and solar, among others. Roof replacement and basement finishing are not listed on the city's page, so contact the Building Official or the inspection hotline at 515-978-9533 to confirm.

Other items to know:

  • As of April 1, 2024, Community Development no longer issues irrigation meter permits for properties with a certificate of occupancy. Public Works handles those.
  • Underground irrigation systems need a reduced-pressure-zone backflow device.
  • Dog and cat licenses and urban chicken permits are issued through the city.

City Hall's main number is 515-978-7900 and Public Works is 515-978-7920. If previous owners built a deck or fence, check that a permit was pulled before a buyer asks.

sections.h2: How does Waukee compare with Urbandale next door?
sections.html:
Waukee and Urbandale share a border area and some school boundaries, but the Census numbers differ. Waukee's median home value is higher, and its owner-occupancy rate is lower.

A more even split between owners and renters in Waukee matches the amount of new multi-family housing in the city's project list.

sections.h2: What other facts about Waukee residents help a seller?
sections.html:
The 2023 American Community Survey figures cited for Waukee show a median household income of $106,728, a poverty rate of 7.3 percent and 56.7 percent of adults with a bachelor's degree or higher. The 2020 census listed the population as 81.68 percent non-Hispanic White, 5.28 percent Asian, 3.72 percent Black and 5.23 percent Hispanic or Latino.

With a median age of 33.9, many owners are in earlier career stages, and a job move is one common reason people sell.

sections.h2: What documents should a Waukee seller gather?
sections.html:
• Your latest Dallas County tax statement and proof of the first-half and second-half payments.
  • Any permit records for decks, fences, additions or pools.
  • Mortgage payoff statement and the names on the title.
  • Plat and covenant details if your lot is in an association.

Your closing agent orders the title work. Having these items ready helps with any sale route.

sections.h2: How do property tax and transfer tax work for a Waukee sale?
sections.html:
Dallas County collects property tax in two installments, due September 1 and March 1 and delinquent after September 30 and March 31. Interest is 1.5 percent per month, and the postmark is the only mailing date the county recognizes. The Treasurer's office is at 800 Court Street, Suite 111, in Adel, and its phone number is 515-993-5808.

Iowa's transfer tax is 80 cents per $500 of value after the first $500. Using the Waukee median of $350,500, that works out to $560.00 by our math. A declaration of value is signed by a seller, buyer or agent and filed with the recorder with the deed.

Iowa Code 558A.4 sets what a seller's disclosure statement covers, including significant structural defects and lead service lines. Ask your closing agent what applies to your sale.

sections.h2: What choices do Waukee sellers have?
sections.html:
A traditional listing can suit a well-kept house in a fast-growing market, and you will pay commission and wait for a buyer's financing. Selling yourself saves commission. A cash sale suits owners who inherited, own a rental, or do not want to spend on repairs, and it removes the lender step.

Ask each option for a written net figure and closing date.

faqs.q: Which county handles property tax for Waukee?
faqs.a: Dallas County. The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1, with interest of 1.5 percent per month after each deadline.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a deck or fence in Waukee?
faqs.a: Yes. Both are on the city's building permit list and are submitted through the online portal.
The 2020 census counted 23,940 people, and the 2024 estimate is 34,420, which makes Waukee the 16th-largest city in Iowa.

faqs.q: What is a typical home value in Waukee?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists a median of $350,500 for owner-occupied homes from 2020 to 2024. Your own house may sit above or below that.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Waukee houses?
faqs.a: The Waukee Community School District covers about 55 square miles and includes parts of Clive, Urbandale and West Des Moines, so check your address with the district.
